questions.q: Why is clean_trips(df) easier to unit test than process_trips(), which reads a file and transforms it in one function?
options: There's no real testing difference between the two approaches
clean_trips(df) doesn't actually perform any real transformation logic
A function taking a DataFrame in and returning one out can be handed exactly the test data you want, without needing a real file to read
process_trips() is impossible to write in PySpark
questions.explain: You can't easily unit-test "reads a file and transforms it" without a real file, but you can easily hand a function a specific DataFrame.

questions.q: Why use master("local[1]") when creating a SparkSession for tests?
options: It disables all DataFrame transformations for safety
It connects directly to the production KQL Database
It runs Spark on a single local thread with no Fabric workspace, real cluster, or network call — fast enough to run dozens of times per commit
It's required for any PySpark code to run at all
questions.explain: This speed is what makes unit tests practical as part of Lesson 45's CI/CD Test stage.

questions.q: Why can naively comparing two DataFrames row-by-row via collect() produce a flaky test?
options: DataFrames can never be compared in any way
Flakiness in this context is always a sign of a real bug, not a test problem
collect() always returns an empty result
Spark distributes work across partitions with no guaranteed row order, so identical data can come back in a different order each time
questions.explain: Sorting both results by a stable key before comparing avoids this false-failure problem entirely.

questions.q: What does a unit test on a single transformation catch that a full pipeline test (Lesson 48) wouldn't pinpoint as easily?
options: Only row-count problems, never logic errors
Only schema drift, never a genuine logic bug
Nothing — full pipeline tests and unit tests catch exactly the same things
Exactly which specific transformation broke, without needing to debug an entire pipeline run to find it
questions.explain: A full pipeline test tells you the whole thing worked or didn't; a unit test isolates exactly where a failure occurred.

questions.q: What DataFrame operations from DE Foundations Lessons 44-45 does this lesson's testable transformation shape build on?
options: select() and filter()/where()
read.csv() and write.parquet()
join() and groupBy() only
createDataFrame() and toPandas()
questions.explain: The testable version keeps the exact same DataFrame-in, DataFrame-out shape those lessons taught, just isolated from file I/O.
